title: Move smarter
subtitle: Notice how clothing and equipment change movement.
description: Notice how clothing and equipment change movement.

questions.prompt: What is a main purpose of the side splits in running shorts?
answers: To keep the waistband from slipping
To let the legs move more freely
To compress the thigh muscles
To support items in the pockets
questions.hint: Think about what happens to a narrow hem when you lengthen your stride.
questions.explanation: Side splits allow the fabric to separate as the legs move. Elijah secures his cloak before running; that specific clothing adjustment supports an inference about avoiding restricted movement. The narrative attributes his feat to the Lord, not superior sportswear.
questions.authorFinding: Easy proposal. The historic ledger used this same verse for the answer Running; this changes the tested concept to garment construction. Flag deliberate reference reuse, not a wholly fresh passage.
questions.concept: Running clothing and freedom of movement

questions.prompt: During a steady wall sit, how do the thigh muscles mainly work?
answers: They repeatedly shorten and lengthen
They relax between each breath
They maintain tension without much change in length
They stop exerting force once the pose is set
questions.hint: A motionless load can still require muscular effort.
questions.explanation: An isometric contraction produces tension with little change in muscle length. Moses needs support while his arms remain raised; the battle account is not exercise instruction.
questions.authorFinding: Duplicate concept/reference: the historical dumbbell-at-right-angle question already tested isometric action with Exodus 17:12. Do not count a wall-sit reskin as fresh coverage; replace. Distractors also need strengthening.

questions.prompt: Holding the same dumbbell at shoulder height, which position creates the least turning effect about the shoulder?
answers: Arm straight forward, palm down
Elbow bent, weight close to the shoulder
Arm straight out to the side, palm down
Arm straight forward, palm up
questions.hint: Compare the horizontal distance between the weight and the joint.
questions.explanation: The dumbbell produces the smallest gravitational torque when its horizontal distance from the shoulder is smallest. Its weight has not changed. Turning the palm does not change the dumbbell’s horizontal lever arm when the arm position stays the same. The shepherd places the sheep on his shoulders rather than at arm’s length; this supplies the concrete load-placement analogy. Jesus explains joy over repentance, not an exercise prescription.
questions.authorFinding: Replaces the impossible mass/air distractors with achievable holding positions. All weights are at shoulder height; bringing the weight close reduces its horizontal lever arm. Palm orientation is a plausible but irrelevant variable for the weight’s gravitational torque. Tests external dumbbell torque only, not the total muscular effort including arm weight.

lineage.reason: Replace impossible distractors with real positions; ask about external torque explicitly.

questions.prompt: In a wet-floor version of this footing problem, how can shoe-tread channels help?
answers: By giving the ankle more support
By draining liquid from beneath the sole
By cushioning the heel’s impact
By keeping the foot cooler
questions.hint: Think of the grooves on a car tire in rain.
questions.explanation: Tread channels can provide a route for liquid to escape from the shoe-floor interface, limiting the fluid layer that reduces traction. The other choices describe different footwear functions. Psalm 94 uses slipping and support to express reliance on God amid wrongdoing; the wet floor is an explicitly imagined modern comparison, not the setting asserted by the verse.
questions.authorFinding: Replaces held bicycle-gearing analogy to a dull axe. Four real footwear functions; tread drainage rather than cushioning is the intended distinction. Reading supplies a slipping-foot image, but it does not explain tread or specify wetness: that bridge remains the main review risk. Tire clue adds a familiar parallel without repeating the answer. Do not claim any tread guarantees traction, or generalize one material/pattern across all surfaces and contaminants. Near-context moral danger is preserved. Distinct from Challenger lateral stance width and accepted strap-pressure question.
questions.concept: Shoe tread drainage and wet-floor traction
questions.coordinatorFinding: Impossible distractors and axe sharpening is not the gearing tradeoff; replace pairing or question.

questions.prompt: As an ordinary elastic exercise band is stretched farther within its working range, what usually happens to its pull?
answers: It gradually weakens
It stays exactly constant
It gradually increases
It disappears once the band is taut
questions.hint: The material resists being pulled away from its resting shape.
questions.explanation: Elastic band tension generally increases with elongation. The bow image associates drawing a resistant object with strength. Psalm 18 credits God with deliverance and martial strength; it does not establish an elastic-band force curve or a literal bronze-bow construction.
questions.authorFinding: Hold: bow-strength imagery alone does not establish increasing resistance, and the disappearance distractor is weak. PMC full-page access returned a challenge; manufacturer evidence was accessible. Do not claim linearity, universal band specifications, or measured hint benefit.
